skill.name: project-testing
skill.description: Provides reusable guidance for project-specific unit, integration, and end-to-end tests with fixtures, mocks, naming conventions, coverage targets, and CI scope.
skill.summary: Guide AI assistants to create isolated, maintainable project tests using consistent fixtures, mocks, naming rules, and coverage expectations.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and a fenced Python example in SKILL.md. The reviewed file provides testing guidance only, with no executable shell commands, prompt injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or malicious workflow.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 43 uses Markdown inline code to document the tests/unit/ folder path. It is not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 52 uses Markdown inline code to document the tests/integration/ folder path. There is no command invocation or user-controlled execution.
Line 61 uses Markdown inline code to document e2e test locations. It describes file paths and does not execute commands.
Line 72 uses Markdown inline code to document the tests/fixtures/ folder path. No shell or Ruby evaluation is present.
Line 75 starts a fenced Python documentation example. The backticks are Markdown formatting, not an executable shell construct.
Line 82 closes the fenced documentation block. It is Markdown syntax only and cannot execute commands.
Line 86 uses Markdown inline code to document the tests/mocks/ folder path. It is a static path reference, not a command.
Line 95 shows unit test file and function naming patterns inside a Markdown table. The backticks only format examples.
Line 96 shows integration test naming patterns in Markdown inline code. There is no executable context or command expansion.
Line 97 documents an E2E file pattern and test title format. The inline backticks are Markdown formatting, not shell execution.

content.value_statement: Teams often write inconsistent tests that are hard to maintain. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a shared testing structure for fixtures, mocks, coverage, and CI scope.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requested tests as unit, integration, or end-to-end work.
Points assistants toward documented fixture and mock locations.
Defines naming conventions for unit, integration, and E2E test files.
Promotes isolation, cleanup, and fixture-based test data.
Summarizes coverage targets for core logic, API routes, and utilities.
Describes which test groups should run on pull requests, merges, and nightly jobs.
limitations: It is a template and still contains project placeholders.
It does not include runnable test commands or framework configuration.
It does not define real project fixtures or mock services.
It cannot verify coverage results without the project test runner.

use_cases.title: Create focused unit tests
use_cases.description: Use the skill to keep generated unit tests isolated, fast, and aligned with local naming rules.

use_cases.title: Plan integration coverage
use_cases.description: Use the skill to structure tests around component interactions, database fixtures, and cleanup expectations.

use_cases.title: Standardize QA workflows
use_cases.description: Use the skill to align E2E tests, coverage targets, and CI test groups across a project.

prompt_templates.title: Choose test type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for classifying a testing request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-testing skill. Decide whether this should be a unit, integration, or E2E test, then explain the test scope.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a unit test plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic prompt for a single function or method.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-testing skill to plan unit tests for this function. Include isolation needs, fixtures, naming, and cleanup checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design integration tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-testing skill to design integration tests for this workflow. Identify fixtures, mock services, database setup, and expected cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Build a release test strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for broad test planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-testing skill to create a release test strategy. Cover unit, integration, E2E, coverage targets, CI timing, and flake risks.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for an order creation feature.
output: The assistant separates unit tests for validation from integration tests for persistence.
It recommends reusable user and order fixtures.
It includes cleanup requirements and coverage targets.

output_examples.input: Review an E2E test proposal for checkout.
output: The assistant checks whether the proposal covers the full user workflow.
It flags timing-dependent steps that could become flaky.
It recommends CI placement for pull requests, merges, or nightly runs.

output_examples.input: Standardize test file names for a new module.
output_examples.output: The assistant maps each test type to the documented naming pattern and explains where each file should live.

best_practices: Replace template placeholders with real project paths before relying on the skill.
Provide the code or workflow under test when asking for test plans.
Ask the assistant to state cleanup and isolation assumptions for every test.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as a substitute for running the actual test suite.
Do not accept generated tests that depend on execution order or fixed timing.
Do not keep placeholder fixture and mock names in production test guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing guidance and structure, but it does not execute a test runner.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it generate real test files?
faq.answer: It can guide an assistant while drafting tests, but project code and framework details are still required.

faq.question: Does it include project-specific fixtures?
faq.answer: No. The skill references fixture and mock locations, but it leaves real definitions for the project team.

faq.question: Is it useful for E2E testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes E2E location guidance, workflow expectations, timeout context, and CI placement guidance.

faq.question: What should be customized first?
faq.answer: Update placeholders, fixture lists, mock services, and coverage exceptions for the target project.
